title: CocoRNA: Collective RNA Design with Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

old.gist: CocoRNA decomposes RNA inverse design into sub-problems solved by cooperating agents trained with a centralized critic, reporting higher success rate and speed than prior methods on Rfam.

new.gist: The authors design RNA sequences that fold into target shapes by splitting the task among cooperating agents. On Rfam structures, it beats prior approaches in success rate and speed.

title: Waiting Buys Exactly Two Moments: Endogenous Identification in Prediction-Driven Allocation

old.gist: Shows a length-τ observation prefix identifies exactly the latent risk moments up to order 2τ−1, buying two per period; timing regret is unavoidable at fixed observation length.

new.gist: Waiting reveals risk but removes high-risk people from treatment, making the timing of help a tradeoff. Observing for t periods identifies exactly 2t moments of hidden risk, so some timing errors cannot be removed.

title: Rethinking the design space of Vanilla Pixel Diffusion Transformers

old.gist: Introduces MFlow, an adaptive parameterization that learns to blend x0- and u-prediction in pixel diffusion transformers, and ConvRefiner, a post-hoc adversarial module that restores high-frequency detail.

new.gist: The paper tunes how pixel-space diffusion transformers predict their targets, learning a blend of clean-image and velocity prediction, and adds a convolutional module that restores lost high-frequency detail.

title: Interaction-Limited Safe Continuous-Time RL for Dynamical Medical Treatment

old.gist: Proposes an option-based semi-Markov formulation for continuous-time medical treatment that jointly learns treatment and interaction timing under trajectory safety constraints, with guarantees and experiments beating equidistant schedules.

new.gist: The authors learn treatment dosing and the timing of clinical check-ins jointly, under safety constraints that hold between visits. Learned timing beats fixed schedules on safety and treatment effectiveness.

title: PrismQuant: Optimal Null-Space Rotations for Grouped Quantizers

old.gist: Aligns the leading activation eigenspace with the constant subspace of asymmetric grouped INT4 via closed-form Ky Fan-optimal Householder rotations, reaching state-of-the-art W4A4KV4 accuracy and 1.51x prefill speedup on Llama-3.1-8B.

new.gist: The authors rotate activations so their largest directions align with the shared offsets of 4-bit grouped quantization, reducing accuracy loss and enabling faster, lower-memory inference on Llama models.

title: A Survey of Flow Matching in Reinforcement Learning

old.gist: Surveys flow-matching approaches in reinforcement learning, organizing the literature by modeled target distribution and by how RL signals are integrated, and compares them against Gaussian and diffusion baselines.

new.gist: The authors survey flow-matching methods for reinforcement learning, sorting them by modeled distribution and RL signal, and compare them with Gaussian and diffusion policies.

title: Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment

old.gist: ALMEA addresses missing modalities and cross-graph topology asymmetry in multimodal entity alignment, using imputation, latent calibration, and pseudo-label selection to gain up to 5.20% MRR at 20% supervision.

new.gist: The paper introduces a framework that fills in missing modality features and calibrates joint embeddings across knowledge graphs, raising MRR by up to 5.20% over baselines at 20% supervision.

title: PLDiv: Measuring Dataset Diversity and Semantic Collapse via Persistence Landscapes

old.gist: Proposes PLDiv, a scalar dataset diversity metric built from persistence landscapes of sample embeddings, which tracks semantic collapse in text, image, instruction and reasoning data and performs competitively against baselines.

new.gist: A new diversity metric scores datasets by the shape of how their samples cluster, and performs competitively with existing baselines at detecting semantic collapse.

title: Judging the Judges: Confidence and Disagreement in Rubrics as Rewards

old.gist: Shows the choice of LLM judge shifts rubric-reward training scores, and proposes RaRE, a judge ensemble with logprob-weighted rewards and disagreement masking that beats every single-judge variant.

new.gist: Judge choice shifts reinforcement learning results on medical and science rubrics; a judge ensemble that weights confident judges more beats every single judge on HealthBench and GPQA Diamond.

title: HiLo-Token: Input-Adaptive High-Low Frequency Token Compression for Efficient Image Editing

old.gist: Proposes HiLo-Token, an input-adaptive token compression method for diffusion-transformer image editing that keeps mask-region and high-frequency tokens plus a downsampled background, giving 1.67–3.13× DiT speedups without quality loss.

new.gist: The authors drop most image tokens a diffusion transformer processes in mask-based editing, keeping detail near the edit. On production data this gives 1.67 to 3.13 times faster inference.

title: LLM-HB: Language-Aware LLM-Guided Hotword Biasing for Code-Switching ASR

old.gist: Proposes LLM-HB, an LLM-guided hotword biasing framework with a mixture-of-experts adaptor and language prediction head for code-switching speech recognition, reducing mixed error rate 20.30% relative on ASRU2019.

new.gist: The authors propose LLM-HB, which steers a speech recognizer toward listed hotwords in mixed-language speech. It cuts error 20.30% relative on the ASRU2019 code-switching test set.

old.gist: Introduces operator surrogates, finite-parametric maps approximating nonlinear operators between function spaces, surveying encoder-approximator-decoder designs, spectral and neural architectures, and convergence rates for holomorphic operators.

new.gist: A mathematical introduction to operator surrogates, learned maps that approximate nonlinear maps between function spaces. It surveys encoder-approximator-decoder designs, spectral and neural architectures, and convergence bounds for holomorphic operators.
